# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1707
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1707
- **Title**: fix(1705): boarding flow asks provider before api type
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1705-cli-boarding-flow` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +98
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:19:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T05:09:51Z

## PR Description

## Old order (source trace, repro)

Fresh-install boarding (issue #969 flag) went straight into the custom-provider wizard:

- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` flags the boot `freshInstallProviderFlow`
- `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart) called `_startProviderFlow()` unconditionally
- `runCustomProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_flow.dart:159) opens with **`pickOption('api type', ...)`** — the api-type menu (openai-like / anthropic-like / google-like / minimax-like) is the FIRST question, before the user has named any provider

That is exactly the reported symptom: "Fa asks to choose api type... but it needs to ask /add-provider to choose provider first".

## What changed

The boarding now opens the **provider choice first** — the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (AIIN, OpenRouter, ChatGPT, Copilot, CodeMie, DIAL, Kimi, Z.AI, MiniMax, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Custom last) — and routes the pick exactly like the TUI picker (`_tuiPickAddProvider`):

- **Custom** → the existing api-type wizard (api type still asked, now only where it is relevant)
- **a preset** → its own setup flow; those flows prefill the api type, so the user is never cold-asked it
- **Ctrl-C** → "provider setup cancelled", idle prompt restored (unchanged redraw contract)

New `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_provider_presets.dart) reuses `_addProviderItems()`/`_addProviderHandlers` as the single source of truth, and follows the repo's gate convention (`_handleOpenRouterAuthMethodChoice`): hold `_providerFlowActive` across the pick, release before handoff, clear the line buffer in `finally`. `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` keeps its signature and future-redraw contract.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK, dart 3.13.5)

- `dart analyze` on the three touched Dart files: **No issues found**
- `dart test test/cli/fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart test/cli/provider_flow_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (fresh-install suite extended: happy path now answers the provider pick (Custom = 13) before the api-type pick and pins `indexOf('choose provider') < indexOf('api type')`; cancel test pins the wizard never opened; new test pins that a preset (OpenAI = 10) opens the wizard with its api type preselected `(current)`)
- `dart test test/cli/add_provider_picker_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (picker/handler pairing boarding now rides on)
- `dart format` clean on touched files

No CI was dispatched or rerunned (owner owns scheduling).

blocks.text:
Now I've read the whole `agent_cli_provider_presets.dart`. Key observations:

1. `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` — new method. It:
  - Checks `_providerFlowActive` gate
  - Sets gate to true
  - Shows provider pick with all `_addProviderItems()` — mapping `preset:X` keys to `X`
  - Releases gate before handoff
  - choice == null → "provider setup cancelled"
  - choice == 'custom' → `_startProviderFlow()`
  - else → `_addProviderHandlers[choice]?.call()`
  - finally: gate false + `_promptLineBuffer.clear()`

Potential issues:

**Issue A: silent no-op when a handler is missing.** `await _addProviderHandlers[choice]?.call();` — if a preset item exists in `_addProviderItems()` but has no handler in `_addProviderHandlers`, the choice silently does nothing. But the doc comment on `_addProviderItems` says "Every `preset:<name>` key MUST have a matching entry in `_addProviderHandlers` — the picker used to ship without Copilot even though `/provider copilot` worked, because this list is hand-maintained (the test asserts the pairing)." So the pairing test (`add_provider_picker_test.dart`) covers this. So the `?.` is consistent with `_tuiPickAddProvider` which uses the same `?.call()`. OK, low priority.

**Issue B: `choice` values.** `_pickOption` returns the key. For custom, key = 'custom'. For presets, key = 'ain', 'openrouter', etc. This matches the handler map keys. Good.

**Issue C: gate release before `_pickOption` completes?** No — the gate is held during the pick and released after the pick resolves, before dispatching to the sub-flow. That matches `_kimiResolvedKeyChoice` convention (`_providerFlowActive = false; _startProviderFlow(...)`). Good.

**Issue D: The `finally` block clears `_promptLineBuffer` and resets the gate even in the cancelled path.** That matches `_handleKimiCommand` convention.

**Issue E: What about `_tuiPickAddProvider` reuse?** `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` duplicates the routing logic of `_tuiPickAddProvider` (custom → `_startProviderFlow`, else handlers[choice]). But it cannot call `_tuiPickAddProvider` directly because it needs to release the gate before dispatching (whereas `_tuiPickAddProvider` runs inside the TUI picker context where the gate isn't held). Hmm — actually wait, could it? `_tuiPickAddProvider` for custom calls `return _startProviderFlow()` — `_startProviderFlow` takes its own gate. If called while `_providerFlowActive` is true, `_startProviderFlow` would return early (silently do nothing). So the gate release is needed before the handoff, so `_tuiPickAddProvider` cannot be reused as-is while holding the gate. The comment explains this. It's a small duplication (2 lines of routing); acceptable but could be noted as suggestion.

**Issue F: numbering / key display.** The test says '13' is Custom. 13 items → indices 1..13. OK.

**Issue G: `io.writeln('choose a provider to set up (Ctrl-C to skip)')` — then `_pickOption('choose provider', ...)`. Consistent with other flows.

Now the more important question: **What is `_pickOption`?** Need to check the signature — `_pickOption(title, options, initialKey: ...)` where options are `(key, label, description)` records. Let me check.

**Issue H: headless/piped guard.** `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` checks `io.isInteractive`. OK unchanged.

**Issue I: The boarding flow previously returned `_startProviderFlow()` future; now returns `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice()` future. The doc says "Returns the flow's future (null when the boot is not fresh) so the line-mode entry can redraw the idle prompt when it settles". Fine.

**Issue J: What about the case where the user picks a preset whose flow itself returns early due to gate?** E.g., picking a preset while `_providerFlowActive` is somehow true. The gate is released before handoff, so sub-flows can take it. OK.

**Issue K: Error paths — what if `_addProviderHandlers[choice]` is a OAuth flow (e.g., openrouter OAuth)? In CLI mode (not TUI), do these flows work in line mode? The boarding is line-mode (REPL answers prompts). `_handleOpenRouterAuthMethodChoice` — is it line-compatible? The test suite only covers custom (13) and openai preset (10). OAuth flows might use `_pickOption` too. Since it's the same REPL mechanics, presumably fine. But hmm — some flows like ChatGPT OAuth (`_handleChatGptOAuthCommand(headless: false)`) and Copilot device flow print URLs and poll; in a fresh-install boot these may be weird but they're user-triggered choices. Not blocking.

**Issue L: `item.key.substring('preset:'.length)` — fine.

Now the diff shows the CHANGELOG entry — check CHANGELOG heading context. The entry is added under `## Unreleased`. Fine.

Wait — one important check: the diff at the top says `@@ -13,6 +13,13 @@ block a release again.` — the `## Unreleased` section. The new entry is inserted as the first bullet of Unreleased. Fine.

**Issue M: The test change for cancel path.** Previously Ctrl-C on the first question → 'custom provider setup cancelled'. Now Ctrl-C on the provider pick → 'provider setup cancelled'. The test waits for 'provider setup cancelled' and asserts 'custom provider setup' never appears. Good.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

(store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is

`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

- **Title**: fix(1705): boarding flow asks provider before api type
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1705-cli-boarding-flow` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +98
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:19:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T05:09:51Z

## PR Description

## Old order (source trace, repro)

Fresh-install boarding (issue #969 flag) went straight into the custom-provider wizard:

- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` flags the boot `freshInstallProviderFlow`
- `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart) called `_startProviderFlow()` unconditionally
- `runCustomProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_flow.dart:159) opens with **`pickOption('api type', ...)`** — the api-type menu (openai-like / anthropic-like / google-like / minimax-like) is the FIRST question, before the user has named any provider

That is exactly the reported symptom: "Fa asks to choose api type... but it needs to ask /add-provider to choose provider first".

## What changed

The boarding now opens the **provider choice first** — the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (AIIN, OpenRouter, ChatGPT, Copilot, CodeMie, DIAL, Kimi, Z.AI, MiniMax, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Custom last) — and routes the pick exactly like the TUI picker (`_tuiPickAddProvider`):

- **Custom** → the existing api-type wizard (api type still asked, now only where it is relevant)
- **a preset** → its own setup flow; those flows prefill the api type, so the user is never cold-asked it
- **Ctrl-C** → "provider setup cancelled", idle prompt restored (unchanged redraw contract)

New `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_provider_presets.dart) reuses `_addProviderItems()`/`_addProviderHandlers` as the single source of truth, and follows the repo's gate convention (`_handleOpenRouterAuthMethodChoice`): hold `_providerFlowActive` across the pick, release before handoff, clear the line buffer in `finally`. `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` keeps its signature and future-redraw contract.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK, dart 3.13.5)

- `dart analyze` on the three touched Dart files: **No issues found**
- `dart test test/cli/fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart test/cli/provider_flow_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (fresh-install suite extended: happy path now answers the provider pick (Custom = 13) before the api-type pick and pins `indexOf('choose provider') < indexOf('api type')`; cancel test pins the wizard never opened; new test pins that a preset (OpenAI = 10) opens the wizard with its api type preselected `(current)`)
- `dart test test/cli/add_provider_picker_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (picker/handler pairing boarding now rides on)
- `dart format` clean on touched files

No CI was dispatched or rerunned (owner owns scheduling).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. - **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T05:09:51Z

## PR Description

## Old order (source trace, repro)

Fresh-install boarding (issue #969 flag) went straight into the custom-provider wizard:

- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` flags the boot `freshInstallProviderFlow`
- `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart) called `_startProviderFlow()` unconditionally
- `runCustomProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_flow.dart:159) opens with **`pickOption('api type', ...)`** — the api-type menu (openai-like / anthropic-like / google-like / minimax-like) is the FIRST question, before the user has named any provider

That is exactly the reported symptom: "Fa asks to choose api type... but it needs to ask /add-provider to choose provider first".

## What changed

The boarding now opens the **provider choice first** — the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (AIIN, OpenRouter, ChatGPT, Copilot, CodeMie, DIAL, Kimi, Z.AI, MiniMax, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Custom last) — and routes the pick exactly like the TUI picker (`_tuiPickAddProvider`):

- **Custom** → the existing api-type wizard (api type still asked, now only where it is relevant)
- **a preset** → its own setup flow; those flows prefill the api type, so the user is never cold-asked it
- **Ctrl-C** → "provider setup cancelled", idle prompt restored (unchanged redraw contract)

New `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_provider_presets.dart) reuses `_addProviderItems()`/`_addProviderHandlers` as the single source of truth, and follows the repo's gate convention (`_handleOpenRouterAuthMethodChoice`): hold `_providerFlowActive` across the pick, release before handoff, clear the line buffer in `finally`. `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` keeps its signature and future-redraw contract.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK, dart 3.13.5)

- `dart analyze` on the three touched Dart files: **No issues found**
- `dart test test/cli/fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart test/cli/provider_flow_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (fresh-install suite extended: happy path now answers the provider pick (Custom = 13) before the api-type pick and pins `indexOf('choose provider') < indexOf('api type')`; cancel test pins the wizard never opened; new test pins that a preset (OpenAI = 10) opens the wizard with its api type preselected `(current)`)
- `dart test test/cli/add_provider_picker_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (picker/handler pairing boarding now rides on)
- `dart format` clean on touched files

No CI was dispatched or rerunned (owner owns scheduling).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release

  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(#1705): CLI fresh-install boarding asks the provider choice FIRST —
  the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (presets, `Custom` last) —
  and only `Custom` continues into the api-type wizard; a preset opens its
  own flow with the api type prefilled. Previously boarding opened the
  custom wizard directly, cold-asking "api type" before any provider was
  chosen.

- feat(bench): gh-1681 — leaderboard submission readiness. ATIF
  trajectories: new `exportAtifJson` whole-snapshot exporter
  (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, ATIF-v1.7 — the schema harbor
  0.23.0's flagship adapters emit) behind a headless `fa trajectory
  export [--format atif] [--output path]` verb; the harbor adapter runs
  it as a bounded best-effort exec after the agent phase on every
  terminal path, so `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` reaches the hub with
  the other agent logs (the leaderboard static analysis requires one per
  rewarded trial) and `result.json` metadata carries an
  `atif_trajectory` present/missing marker. The golden fixture
  (`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json`) is pinned Dart-side and
  cross-validated against harbor's pydantic `Trajectory` +
  `validate_trajectory` in `test_atif_contract.py`. Workflow: a
  `submission: true` dispatch input turns the submission rules into hard
  setup preflights (full task coverage, ≥5 attempts/task, no
  agent-timeout override, pinned dataset) and makes the new per-shard
  ATIF presence gate fail hard; default runs gain only a warn-only scan

  `runHeadless`' finally and the REPL teardown as the LAST session action

  paths — REG-2), it makes every writer (`_persistMessages`,

  writer class — never a throw into an unhandled zone; the exit code
  stays the turn's terminal outcome (issue #413 semantics untouched). The

  raises a fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) so a background-shell settle or
  task completion arriving after the final answer's drain — including the
  registry's one-turn-deferred listener racing `_finishHeadlessDrain`'s

  seal is per-run state, so resume/replay/`session_repair` are unchanged.

Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Updated**: 2026-10-20T05:09:51Z

## PR Description

## Old order (source trace, repro)

Fresh-install boarding (issue #969 flag) went straight into the custom-provider wizard:

- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` flags the boot `freshInstallProviderFlow`
- `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart) called `_startProviderFlow()` unconditionally
- `runCustomProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_flow.dart:159) opens with **`pickOption('api type', ...)`** — the api-type menu (openai-like / anthropic-like / google-like / minimax-like) is the FIRST question, before the user has named any provider

That is exactly the reported symptom: "Fa asks to choose api type... but it needs to ask /add-provider to choose provider first".

## What changed

The boarding now opens the **provider choice first** — the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (AIIN, OpenRouter, ChatGPT, Copilot, CodeMie, DIAL, Kimi, Z.AI, MiniMax, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Custom last) — and routes the pick exactly like the TUI picker (`_tuiPickAddProvider`):

- **Custom** → the existing api-type wizard (api type still asked, now only where it is relevant)
- **a preset** → its own setup flow; those flows prefill the api type, so the user is never cold-asked it
- **Ctrl-C** → "provider setup cancelled", idle prompt restored (unchanged redraw contract)

New `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_provider_presets.dart) reuses `_addProviderItems()`/`_addProviderHandlers` as the single source of truth, and follows the repo's gate convention (`_handleOpenRouterAuthMethodChoice`): hold `_providerFlowActive` across the pick, release before handoff, clear the line buffer in `finally`. `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` keeps its signature and future-redraw contract.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK, dart 3.13.5)

- `dart analyze` on the three touched Dart files: **No issues found**
- `dart test test/cli/fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart test/cli/provider_flow_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (fresh-install suite extended: happy path now answers the provider pick (Custom = 13) before the api-type pick and pins `indexOf('choose provider') < indexOf('api type')`; cancel test pins the wizard never opened; new test pins that a preset (OpenAI = 10) opens the wizard with its api type preselected `(current)`)
- `dart test test/cli/add_provider_picker_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (picker/handler pairing boarding now rides on)
- `dart format` clean on touched files

No CI was dispatched or rerunned (owner owns scheduling).

Now I've read the whole `agent_cli_provider_presets.dart`. Key observations:

1. `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` — new method. It:
  - Checks `_providerFlowActive` gate
  - Sets gate to true
  - Shows provider pick with all `_addProviderItems()` — mapping `preset:X` keys to `X`
  - Releases gate before handoff
  - choice == null → "provider setup cancelled"
  - choice == 'custom' → `_startProviderFlow()`
  - else → `_addProviderHandlers[choice]?.call()`
  - finally: gate false + `_promptLineBuffer.clear()`

Potential issues:

**Issue A: silent no-op when a handler is missing.** `await _addProviderHandlers[choice]?.call();` — if a preset item exists in `_addProviderItems()` but has no handler in `_addProviderHandlers`, the choice silently does nothing. But the doc comment on `_addProviderItems` says "Every `preset:<name>` key MUST have a matching entry in `_addProviderHandlers` — the picker used to ship without Copilot even though `/provider copilot` worked, because this list is hand-maintained (the test asserts the pairing)." So the pairing test (`add_provider_picker_test.dart`) covers this. So the `?.` is consistent with `_tuiPickAddProvider` which uses the same `?.call()`. OK, low priority.

**Issue B: `choice` values.** `_pickOption` returns the key. For custom, key = 'custom'. For presets, key = 'ain', 'openrouter', etc. This matches the handler map keys. Good.

**Issue C: gate release before `_pickOption` completes?** No — the gate is held during the pick and released after the pick resolves, before dispatching to the sub-flow. That matches `_kimiResolvedKeyChoice` convention (`_providerFlowActive = false; _startProviderFlow(...)`). Good.

**Issue D: The `finally` block clears `_promptLineBuffer` and resets the gate even in the cancelled path.** That matches `_handleKimiCommand` convention.

**Issue E: What about `_tuiPickAddProvider` reuse?** `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` duplicates the routing logic of `_tuiPickAddProvider` (custom → `_startProviderFlow`, else handlers[choice]). But it cannot call `_tuiPickAddProvider` directly because it needs to release the gate before dispatching (whereas `_tuiPickAddProvider` runs inside the TUI picker context where the gate isn't held). Hmm — actually wait, could it? `_tuiPickAddProvider` for custom calls `return _startProviderFlow()` — `_startProviderFlow` takes its own gate. If called while `_providerFlowActive` is true, `_startProviderFlow` would return early (silently do nothing). So the gate release is needed before the handoff, so `_tuiPickAddProvider` cannot be reused as-is while holding the gate. The comment explains this. It's a small duplication (2 lines of routing); acceptable but could be noted as suggestion.

**Issue F: numbering / key display.** The test says '13' is Custom. 13 items → indices 1..13. OK.

**Issue G: `io.writeln('choose a provider to set up (Ctrl-C to skip)')` — then `_pickOption('choose provider', ...)`. Consistent with other flows.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Does not block merge. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1707
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1707
- **Title**: fix(1705): boarding flow asks provider before api type
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1705-cli-boarding-flow` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +98
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:19:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T05:09:51Z

## PR Description

## Old order (source trace, repro)

Fresh-install boarding (issue #969 flag) went straight into the custom-provider wizard:

- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` flags the boot `freshInstallProviderFlow`
- `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart) called `_startProviderFlow()` unconditionally
- `runCustomProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_flow.dart:159) opens with **`pickOption('api type', ...)`** — the api-type menu (openai-like / anthropic-like / google-like / minimax-like) is the FIRST question, before the user has named any provider

That is exactly the reported symptom: "Fa asks to choose api type... but it needs to ask /add-provider to choose provider first".

## What changed

The boarding now opens the **provider choice first** — the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (AIIN, OpenRouter, ChatGPT, Copilot, CodeMie, DIAL, Kimi, Z.AI, MiniMax, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Custom last) — and routes the pick exactly like the TUI picker (`_tuiPickAddProvider`):

- **Custom** → the existing api-type wizard (api type still asked, now only where it is relevant)
- **a preset** → its own setup flow; those flows prefill the api type, so the user is never cold-asked it
- **Ctrl-C** → "provider setup cancelled", idle prompt restored (unchanged redraw contract)

New `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_provider_presets.dart) reuses `_addProviderItems()`/`_addProviderHandlers` as the single source of truth, and follows the repo's gate convention (`_handleOpenRouterAuthMethodChoice`): hold `_providerFlowActive` across the pick, release before handoff, clear the line buffer in `finally`. `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` keeps its signature and future-redraw contract.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK, dart 3.13.5)

- `dart analyze` on the three touched Dart files: **No issues found**
- `dart test test/cli/fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart test/cli/provider_flow_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (fresh-install suite extended: happy path now answers the provider pick (Custom = 13) before the api-type pick and pins `indexOf('choose provider') < indexOf('api type')`; cancel test pins the wizard never opened; new test pins that a preset (OpenAI = 10) opens the wizard with its api type preselected `(current)`)
- `dart test test/cli/add_provider_picker_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (picker/handler pairing boarding now rides on)
- `dart format` clean on touched files

No CI was dispatched or rerunned (owner owns scheduling).

**Issue A: silent no-op when a handler is missing.** `await _addProviderHandlers[choice]?.call();` — if a preset item exists in `_addProviderItems()` but has no handler in `_addProviderHandlers`, the choice silently does nothing. But the doc comment on `_addProviderItems` says "Every `preset:<name>` key MUST have a matching entry in `_addProviderHandlers` — the picker used to ship without Copilot even though `/provider copilot` worked, because this list is hand-maintained (the test asserts the pairing)." So the pairing test (`add_provider_picker_test.dart`) covers this. So the `?.` is consistent with `_tuiPickAddProvider` which uses the same `?.call()`. OK, low priority.

**Issue B: `choice` values.** `_pickOption` returns the key. For custom, key = 'custom'. For presets, key = 'ain', 'openrouter', etc. This matches the handler map keys. Good.

**Issue C: gate release before `_pickOption` completes?** No — the gate is held during the pick and released after the pick resolves, before dispatching to the sub-flow. That matches `_kimiResolvedKeyChoice` convention (`_providerFlowActive = false; _startProviderFlow(...)`). Good.

**Issue D: The `finally` block clears `_promptLineBuffer` and resets the gate even in the cancelled path.** That matches `_handleKimiCommand` convention.

**Issue E: What about `_tuiPickAddProvider` reuse?** `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` duplicates the routing logic of `_tuiPickAddProvider` (custom → `_startProviderFlow`, else handlers[choice]). But it cannot call `_tuiPickAddProvider` directly because it needs to release the gate before dispatching (whereas `_tuiPickAddProvider` runs inside the TUI picker context where the gate isn't held). Hmm — actually wait, could it? `_tuiPickAddProvider` for custom calls `return _startProviderFlow()` — `_startProviderFlow` takes its own gate. If called while `_providerFlowActive` is true, `_startProviderFlow` would return early (silently do nothing). So the gate release is needed before the handoff, so `_tuiPickAddProvider` cannot be reused as-is while holding the gate. The comment explains this. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(#1705): CLI fresh-install boarding asks the provider choice FIRST —
  the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (presets, `Custom` last) —
  and only `Custom` continues into the api-type wizard; a preset opens its
  own flow with the api type prefilled. Previously boarding opened the
  custom wizard directly, cold-asking "api type" before any provider was
  chosen.

- feat(bench): gh-1681 — leaderboard submission readiness. ATIF
  trajectories: new `exportAtifJson` whole-snapshot exporter
  (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, ATIF-v1.7 — the schema harbor
  0.23.0's flagship adapters emit) behind a headless `fa trajectory
  export [--format atif] [--output path]` verb; the harbor adapter runs
  it as a bounded best-effort exec after the agent phase on every
  terminal path, so `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` reaches the hub with
  the other agent logs (the leaderboard static analysis requires one per
  rewarded trial) and `result.json` metadata carries an
  `atif_trajectory` present/missing marker. The golden fixture
  (`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json`) is pinned Dart-side and
  cross-validated against harbor's pydantic `Trajectory` +
  `validate_trajectory` in `test_atif_contract.py`. Workflow: a
  `submission: true` dispatch input turns the submission rules into hard
  setup preflights (full task coverage, ≥5 attempts/task, no
  agent-timeout override, pinned dataset) and makes the new per-shard
  ATIF presence gate fail hard; default runs gain only a warn-only scan
  (artifact flow unchanged). Runbook: docs/leaderboard-submission.md
  (pinned dataset + @latest content-hash recording, quota-window runner
  policy, lb CLI steps).
- fix(headless): gh-1589 — the headless session becomes a SEALED artifact:
  no session-JSONL writes land after the run's agent phase ends. New
  `Session.seal()` (state in the writer, no file-format change): raised in
  `runHeadless`' finally and the REPL teardown as the LAST session action
  (close order: drain → usage fold → seal → exit, one implementation both
  paths — REG-2), it makes every writer (`_persistMessages`,
  `shell_job_registry` snapshots, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`,
  leaf moves) drop late appends with exactly ONE stderr warning per
  writer class — never a throw into an unhandled zone; the exit code
  stays the turn's terminal outcome (issue #413 semantics untouched). The
  settle→reaction path is sealed with the file (I2): the drain wrap-up
  raises a fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) so a background-shell settle or
  task completion arriving after the final answer's drain — including the
  registry's one-turn-deferred listener racing `_finishHeadlessDrain`'s
  check-to-return window (the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst) — does
  board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record.
  An honest drain's records (final answer → seal) stay legal (E7); the
  seal is per-run state, so resume/replay/`session_repair` are unchanged.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1707
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1707
- **Title**: fix(1705): boarding flow asks provider before api type
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1705-cli-boarding-flow` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +98
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:19:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T05:09:51Z

## PR Description

## Old order (source trace, repro)

Fresh-install boarding (issue #969 flag) went straight into the custom-provider wizard:

- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` flags the boot `freshInstallProviderFlow`
- `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart) called `_startProviderFlow()` unconditionally
- `runCustomProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_flow.dart:159) opens with **`pickOption('api type', ...)`** — the api-type menu (openai-like / anthropic-like / google-like / minimax-like) is the FIRST question, before the user has named any provider

That is exactly the reported symptom: "Fa asks to choose api type... but it needs to ask /add-provider to choose provider first".

## What changed

The boarding now opens the **provider choice first** — the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (AIIN, OpenRouter, ChatGPT, Copilot, CodeMie, DIAL, Kimi, Z.AI, MiniMax, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Custom last) — and routes the pick exactly like the TUI picker (`_tuiPickAddProvider`):

- **Custom** → the existing api-type wizard (api type still asked, now only where it is relevant)
- **a preset** → its own setup flow; those flows prefill the api type, so the user is never cold-asked it
- **Ctrl-C** → "provider setup cancelled", idle prompt restored (unchanged redraw contract)

New `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_provider_presets.dart) reuses `_addProviderItems()`/`_addProviderHandlers` as the single source of truth, and follows the repo's gate convention (`_handleOpenRouterAuthMethodChoice`): hold `_providerFlowActive` across the pick, release before handoff, clear the line buffer in `finally`. `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` keeps its signature and future-redraw contract.

# pr-1707: fix(1705): boarding flow asks provider before api type

## Description

## Old order (source trace, repro)

Fresh-install boarding (issue #969 flag) went straight into the custom-provider wizard:

- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` flags the boot `freshInstallProviderFlow`
- `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart) called `_startProviderFlow()` unconditionally
- `runCustomProviderFlow` (lib/src/cli/provider_flow.dart:159) opens with **`pickOption('api type', ...)`** — the api-type menu (openai-like / anthropic-like / google-like / minimax-like) is the FIRST question, before the user has named any provider

That is exactly the reported symptom: "Fa asks to choose api type... but it needs to ask /add-provider to choose provider first".

## What changed

The boarding now opens the **provider choice first** — the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (AIIN, OpenRouter, ChatGPT, Copilot, CodeMie, DIAL, Kimi, Z.AI, MiniMax, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Custom last) — and routes the pick exactly like the TUI picker (`_tuiPickAddProvider`):

- **Custom** → the existing api-type wizard (api type still asked, now only where it is relevant)
- **a preset** → its own setup flow; those flows prefill the api type, so the user is never cold-asked it
- **Ctrl-C** → "provider setup cancelled", idle prompt restored (unchanged redraw contract)

New `_handleFreshInstallProviderChoice` (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_provider_presets.dart) reuses `_addProviderItems()`/`_addProviderHandlers` as the single source of truth, and follows the repo's gate convention (`_handleOpenRouterAuthMethodChoice`): hold `_providerFlowActive` across the pick, release before handoff, clear the line buffer in `finally`. `_maybeStartFreshInstallProviderFlow` keeps its signature and future-redraw contract.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK, dart 3.13.5)

- `dart analyze` on the three touched Dart files: **No issues found**
- `dart test test/cli/fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart test/cli/provider_flow_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (fresh-install suite extended: happy path now answers the provider pick (Custom = 13) before the api-type pick and pins `indexOf('choose provider') < indexOf('api type')`; cancel test pins the wizard never opened; new test pins that a preset (OpenAI = 10) opens the wizard with its api type preselected `(current)`)
- `dart test test/cli/add_provider_picker_test.dart` — **All tests passed** (picker/handler pairing boarding now rides on)
- `dart format` clean on touched files
